answer: The voyage detector writes to zenith, and terrace makes public every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 189 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 87 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
